name: icecast
why: A streaming audio server with a long internet-radio history is a door into how live audio streams are served over HTTP.

brief.what_it_is: Icecast is free server software that takes live or prerecorded audio and video streams from a source and serves them to listeners over HTTP. According to its homepage it currently supports Ogg (Vorbis and Theora), Opus, WebM and MP3 streams. It can run an internet radio station, a private jukebox, or something in between. The homepage does not describe the input protocol or the listener-facing URLs in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a general-purpose streaming media server: it can be used to create an Internet radio station or a privately running jukebox and many things in between. It is also described as versatile, with new formats addable relatively easily and support for open standards for communication and interaction.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says new formats can be added relatively easily and that the server supports open standards for communication and interaction. It does not explain the streaming mechanism in detail on the pages I read. The docs index points to version-specific documentation for 2.4.x and an unstable 2.5.0 docs page marked WIP.
brief.install_notes: The homepage and docs index give no install commands, runtime requirements, or first-run steps. The Icecast 2.5.0-rc2 news item mentions an updated Icecast installer and run helper on Windows. The 2.5.x series reads Icecast 2.4.x configuration files, so upgrades should be seamless according to the 2.4.4 end-of-support news item. The download page was not fetched.
brief.standout: Xiph.org's streaming server, with a long lineage in internet radio, that serves several open codecs (Ogg Vorbis/Theora, Opus, WebM, MP3) from one server rather than only MP3. It sits in the Xiph.org family alongside Opus, FLAC, Vorbis, Theora, Speex and XSPF.
brief.status: Maintained. Icecast 2.5.0 was released Dec 31, 2025, with an rc2 on Dec 14, 2025. A libigloo 0.9.5 release was posted Dec 31, 2025, and a news item posted Jan 4, 2026 announces end of support for 2.4.4 on 2026-12-31. The homepage copyright reads 2004-2026. I did not check the commit history or the release tags.
brief.caveats: The brew description says 'Streaming MP3 audio server', but the homepage says the server supports Ogg, Opus, WebM and MP3, so MP3 is not the only format. The 2.5.0 docs are marked WIP on the docs page. Icecast 2.4.4 receives only security fixes now and support ends 2026-12-31. The license is GNU GPL version 2. Some older docs listed on the docs page are described as unofficial and possibly outdated. The homepage gives no platform list beyond a Windows installer mention.
quotes: Icecast is free server software for streaming multimedia.
It can be used to create an Internet radio station or a privately running jukebox and many things in between.
Icecast is distributed under the GNU GPL, version 2.
fetch_log: https://icecast.org/ - worked, returned homepage with about section and news
https://icecast.org/docs/ - worked, returned documentation index with version-specific docs and an unstable 2.5.0 WIP link

judge.reason: A hands-on internet-radio server opens up live HTTP streaming, mountpoints, and stream metadata—an overlooked media protocol, not just another file server.

entry.title: Icecast
entry.tldr: Free server software from Xiph.org that takes an audio stream from a source and serves it to listeners over HTTP, the machinery behind many internet radio stations.
entry.deeper_look:
Icecast takes live or prerecorded audio and video from a source and serves it to listeners over HTTP. Its homepage says it supports Ogg (Vorbis and Theora), Opus, WebM and MP3. It can run an internet radio station, a private jukebox, or something in between.

It comes from Xiph.org, the group behind Opus, FLAC, Vorbis, Theora, Speex and XSPF, and has a long history in internet radio. The homepage describes it as versatile: new formats can be added relatively easily, and it supports open standards for communication and interaction.

The idea underneath is that a radio station can be an ordinary web server holding a long-lived connection open. A source client sends audio in, the server relays it to however many listeners connect, and nothing needs special infrastructure. The homepage and docs index do not spell out the input protocol or listener URLs, so the version-specific docs are the place to learn those details.

The brew description says 'Streaming MP3 audio server', which undersells it. MP3 is only one of several formats it handles.
entry.install:
brew install icecast
# The brief gives no first-run steps. You will also need a source client to send audio in, and the docs for your version explain configuration.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the server's command-line options, the safest first look since the brief lists no other commands.

entry.whats_unique: It serves several open codecs (Ogg Vorbis/Theora, Opus, WebM) alongside MP3 from one server, and it belongs to the Xiph.org family of open media formats.
entry.caveats: The 2.5.0 docs are marked WIP, and 2.4.4 gets only security fixes, with support ending 2026-12-31; the brief gives no install or first-run steps.
